Subject: SLA ask: 99.99% & reduced monthly credits for regulated workloads

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Our platform team reviewed the standard Redwood SLA and we have two asks before we can move this through procurement:

1) Uptime: We need a commitment to 99.99% monthly uptime for our production inference endpoints (FinSecure-Prod).
2) Credits: We'd like a narrower service credit band — e.g., only start credits below 99.98% and cap credits at 10% of monthly spend for single-month degradations.

Additionally, because our regulators expect bounded latency, can Redwood include a p95 latency SLO (target) with associated credits if exceeded? We understand this is an exception request, but given the nature of our workloads and the compliance posture, this is a gating item for our procurement/legal.

Please advise whether this is something Redwood can accommodate and what the implementation/ops tradeoffs might be. If useful, I can loop in our platform architect for a short call.

Best,

Ben / Lauren — quick technical read:

High-level thoughts:
- 99.99% (≈ 4.38 min downtime/month) is achievable but not on shared capacity if we want predictable latency SLOs. We'd need a dedicated pool or an isolated routing policy + standby headroom.
- Latency SLO: We can offer a p95 target, but p99 is the more meaningful tail metric for customer-facing services. Recommend committing to p95 < 200ms and p99 < 700ms for the model family they described, with caveats for model version changes and very large sequence lengths.
- Credits: I prefer a sliding credit matrix tied to both uptime and latency violations. Example (quick sketch):
  * Monthly uptime >= 99.98%: no credit
  * 99.95% <= uptime < 99.98%: 5% monthly credit
  * 99.90% <= uptime < 99.95%: 10% monthly credit
  * uptime < 99.90%: 20% monthly credit + incident review
  For latency breaches, small-percentage credits (1–5%) per violation window, aggregated monthly and capped.

Operational points:
- We'll need a canary/fallback policy: if dedicated pool is overloaded, route to a slightly lower-cost variant without data bleed. That needs to be defined in the exception.
- Instrumentation: we need their account to enable extended telemetry (p99 histograms, trace ids) to validate violations; expect a 30-day data retention extension request.

I'll join the call if the FinSecure team wants to walk through details.

Aditya Rao
Head of Infra Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed SLA exception & credit structure for FinSecure-Prod (draft)

Hi Alicia — thanks for your patience. Per our internal review (cc'd Aditya & Lauren), attached is a draft SLA exception we can commit to for FinSecure-Prod. High-level summary below, with our counterproposal on credits and latency: 

1) Uptime commitment: 99.95% monthly for shared-tier; 99.99% monthly if FinSecure purchases Dedicated pool (recommended).
2) Credit matrix (uptime, monthly):
   - >= 99.98%: 0% credit
   - 99.95% — 99.98%: 5% of monthly invoice
   - 99.90% — 99.95%: 12% of monthly invoice
   - < 99.90%: 25% of monthly invoice + executive incident review
3) Latency SLOs (measured on instrumented requests):
   - p95 target: < 200ms — if p95 monthly exceeds target by >20% for two consecutive weeks, 3% credit per month (capped at 10%).
   - p99 target: < 700ms — if p99 exceeds target for two consecutive weeks, additional 5% credit per month (capped together with p95 at 12%).
4) Caps & combined impact: Combined credits (uptime + latency) capped at 30% of monthly invoice. Single-month emergency credits may be considered above this cap by executive review.
5) Operational requirements: Dedicated routing, extended telemetry (30 days), and a jointly maintained mutual action plan for incident playbooks.

I've attached: (A) redwood_sla_exception_draft_v2.pdf — legal-ready wording for our exceptions, and (B) service-credit-matrix.xlsx — numeric examples by invoice size.

If this looks acceptable in principle, legal can prepare a formal amendment and we can send through DocuSign. Would FinSecure like Redwood to draft the amendment or would you prefer to issue your redline?

Next steps suggested:
- FinSecure to confirm whether you will take Dedicated or Shared (impacts uptime commitment).
- If Dedicated, provide estimated QPS and peak hours so we can size pool and include pricing.
- Procurement/legal to indicate process/timeline for DocuSign.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week to walk through the credit math.

—Ben
